# SB-1006 Safety bulletin: hot metal and scale ejection

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Hazard description
This bulletin addresses the hazard of hot metal and scale ejection during handling, quench, and transfer operations associated with the heat treat furnace at line P1-L4. Hot fragments and scale can eject from charge baskets, quench tanks, transfer tooling, or workpiece misorientation and travel trajectories that were not anticipated in task design. These ejections present impact, burn, and inhalation hazards to operators and nearby personnel, and can damage tooling, sensors, and secondary equipment. Ejection events are most likely during charge introduction, agitation of quenchant, basket upset, or when a loose scale fragment or defective restraint becomes a projectile during motion.

Background and rationale
Incidents reviewed in the plant and referenced configuration changes in ECN-2026-015 show a common causal chain: inadequate restraint or containment, delayed quench initiation, and insufficient guard positioning or PPE compliance. The potential energy stored in a high-temperature piece combined with sudden contact with quenchant can cause steam expansion and violent ejection of liquid and solid fragments. To reduce frequency and severity, controls focus on engineering containment, verified sequencing of quench operations, administrative verification steps, and records that demonstrate compliance. Operators and supervisors must understand why each control is required: containment reduces initial trajectory; verified sequencing prevents human error from delaying critical steps; PPE mitigates residual risk when engineering controls cannot eliminate exposure.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) and all associated quench tanks, transfer carts, charge baskets, overhead guarding, and interlocks on line P1-L4. It also applies to loading and unloading stations where parts are staged prior to or after heat treat. Refer to SOP-P1-L4-03 and SOP-P1-L4-05 for procedural interfaces and task boundaries when performing heat treat load/unload and quench operations.

Critical control statement
The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds.

Required controls
Engineering controls
- Containment: Inspect and maintain fixed guards, blast shields, and splash screens around quench tanks and transfer paths. Where removable shields are used, verify retention hardware is present and locked before operation. Design reviews under ECN-2026-015 must be referenced for any modification.
- Quench sequencing: Ensure quench actuation sequence is interlocked to transfer mechanism such that quench initiation occurs automatically at the completion of transfer confirmation. Where manual initiation is allowed per SOP-P1-L4-03, require a two-person verification before initiating quench.
- Transfer restraint: Use dedicated charge baskets and positive retention fixtures designed for the furnace and quenchant. Verify basket latching and alignment sensors are functional before each cycle.

Administrative controls
- Pre-shift inspection: Operators must perform the pre-shift checklist in SOP-P1-L4-05 and annotate any deviations. Items include guard presence, sensor status, basket retention, and clear zone verification.
- Authorized access: Establish exclusion zone protocols around quench tanks during active cycles. Only trained personnel with required PPE may enter a buffered zone during transfer operations.
- Sequencing verification: Record the quench actuation event for every cycle in the log specified by SOP-P1-L4-03. If manual intervention is used, both operator and supervisor must sign the record before part removal.
- Training: All personnel assigned to EQ-P1-L4-HT03 must complete task-specific training covering ejection hazards, emergency shutdown, and the use of PPE. Training completion is documented per SOP-P1-L4-05.

Personal protective equipment
- Mandatory PPE for operators and any personnel within the controlled area includes heat-resistant gloves, face shield, and apron designated for hot metal handling. PPE selection and issuance are recorded in the training and PPE issue records governed by plant policy.

Examples and scenarios
- Example scenario A: A charge basket arrives at the quench tank with a misaligned latch. If transferred without verification, the basket can tip at immersion and eject scale. Prevent by requiring basket latch sensor confirmation and by executing the pre-shift checklist in SOP-P1-L4-05.
- Example scenario B: An operator delays initiation of quench while adjusting positioning. The delay can allow part oxidation and produce a scale fragment that dislodges during immersion. Prevent by enforcing the quench delay maximum and by ensuring automatic sequencing where practical, as specified in ECN-2026-015 and SOP-P1-L4-03.

Operational notes
- Any deviation from the quench sequencing or use of temporary workarounds must be routed through ECN-2026-015 for review and documented in the deviation log referenced in SOP-P1-L4-03. Temporary workarounds without ECN approval are not permitted.
- When maintenance requires removal of guards or disabling interlocks, a lockout-tagout procedure consistent with plant policy must be used and the affected equipment returned to normal configuration and function-verified before resuming production.

Records to keep
- Pre-shift inspection checklists annotated per SOP-P1-L4-05.
- Cycle logs showing quench actuation time and transfer confirmation per SOP-P1-L4-03.
- Training records and PPE issuance for personnel assigned to EQ-P1-L4-HT03.
- Deviation and corrective action records submitted through ECN-2026-015 for any nonconformance or change to controls.
- Incident and near-miss reports involving hot metal or scale ejection, including photographs and root cause analysis.

Implementation and compliance
Supervisors on line P1-L4 are responsible for implementing the controls described herein and for auditing compliance at regular intervals defined in SOP-P1-L4-03. Any observed noncompliance constitutes a stop operation condition until mitigated. Major changes to engineering controls or procedure must be coordinated through the ECN process documented in ECN-2026-015.

Effective date
Effective date: Refer to ECN-2026-015 for the controlled implementation schedule and effective date of procedural changes related to this bulletin.

References
- ECN-2026-015
- SOP-P1-L4-03
- SOP-P1-L4-05
